response: Israeli hospital preparedness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents can be improved by defining surge capacity based on a fixed number of casualties rather than a percentile of bed capacity. This approach may lead to better utilization of national emergency health resources. Additionally, it's been found that only 20% of arriving casualties will require immediate medical treatment, which can help hospitals prepare and allocate resources more effectively. By implementing this concept, hospitals can improve their preparedness and response to terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents.
